# Results — Study 837 (Look-Ahead Standardization): z-scoring with the full sample leaks the future

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py) on **deterministic, offline synthetic
worlds** (base seed 837). This is a research-method demonstration, so the worlds are built on purpose:
the nulls carry **no point-in-time-tradeable edge**, and the control plants a genuine one. Real free
data can never certify "zero edge", so there is no real-tape stamp; the limitation is named on the
SIGNAL axis and the study is capped at `NONE`. Simulation config: **N = 60 names, T = 1,000 days,
forward horizon = 10 days, expanding burn-in = 60, averaged over 20 seeds**. Fingerprint
`5f6dcb4c991c`. As-of **2026-06-30**.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Does full-sample standardisation leak?" `CONFIRMED`

The single most common accidental look-ahead in a feature pipeline is one line:
`z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()` run **once, over the whole sample**, before the train/test split. It
z-scores each feature with statistics that include the *future*. We show — on a world we built to
have **nothing to find** — that this innocuous preprocessing manufactures a large fake Information
Coefficient and a gorgeous fake Sharpe, while the honest **expanding / point-in-time** z-score
(mean & std of the past only) correctly reads ~0.

- **The trap (non-stationary null).** A **random-walk** (price/level-like) feature paired with a
  forward return equal to the feature's own future change over 10 days. Because a random walk's
  increments are iid, the forward return is **genuinely unpredictable from anything known at t** — an
  efficient-market null. Yet **full-sample** standardisation posts a cross-sectional rank IC of
  **−0.138** (Newey-West *t* = **−12.1**) and a fake long-short Sharpe of **15.8**, significant on
  **20 / 20** seeds. The **expanding** z-score on the *same panel* reads IC **−0.000** (*t* = −0.01),
  Sharpe **1.0**, significant on **0 / 20** seeds. The leak manufactures the entire "edge."
- **The contrast (stationary null).** A **stationary** AR(1) feature with iid returns. Here
  full-sample standardisation is (to leading order) a per-name affine rescale, so it barely leaks:
  full IC **−0.000**, expanding IC **+0.000** — both silent. This pins the leak precisely to
  **non-stationarity**, not to standardisation per se.
- **The control (planted real edge).** A stationary feature whose *current* value genuinely predicts
  the next return. The honest **expanding** method recovers IC **+0.091** (*t* = +21.6), significant
  on **20 / 20** seeds — proof the machinery is **unbiased**, not merely always-zero. Its silence on
  the nulls therefore means something.

So `NONE` on the signal axis (a synthetic-only method demo — the only "edge" is a look-ahead
artefact, and there is no real signal to detect), `MIRAGE` on tradability (the fake Sharpe is
**unimplementable** — it needs the full-sample mean/std, i.e. data from *after* every trade — so it
evaporates the instant you standardise point-in-time), and `CONFIRMED` on the myth-check (yes, this
specific leak genuinely breaks inference — by a mile).

## The headline — full-sample vs expanding, three worlds (20 seeds)

| World | Method | Mean IC | IC NW *t* | Fake Sharpe | Significant seeds |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Stationary null** (no leak expected) | full-sample | −0.0004 | −0.06 | 0.37 | 3 / 20 |
| | expanding | +0.0002 | +0.08 | 0.37 | 2 / 20 |
| **Non-stationary null** (THE TRAP) | **full-sample** | **−0.1383** | **−12.12** | **15.84** | **20 / 20** |
| | expanding | −0.0001 | −0.01 | 1.04 | 0 / 20 |
| **Planted real edge** (the control) | full-sample | +0.0922 | +22.79 | 10.61 | 20 / 20 |
| | **expanding** | **+0.0910** | **+21.64** | **10.57** | **20 / 20** |

Read the middle block: on a panel with **provably nothing to find**, full-sample standardisation
prints IC −0.138 (*t* −12) and a Sharpe of ~16 on every single seed, while the point-in-time method
prints zero on every seed. Read the bottom block: the point-in-time method is **not** blind — it lights
up (*t* +22) on a genuine edge. The gap between the two on the trap is the whole story: **|IC| gap
+0.129, Sharpe gap +14.8.**

## The mechanism — why full-sample centring leaks on a random walk

The full-sample mean $\bar x_i = \frac1T\sum_t x_{i,t}$ sits *in the middle of the eventual path*.
Subtracting it, $x_{i,t}-\bar x_i$, tells you whether today is **above or below where the series will
end up on average** — a fact you cannot know at $t$. And a random walk mechanically drifts back toward
its own sample mean, so points below $\bar x_i$ tend to rise and points above tend to fall. The
full-sample-standardised signal has therefore *encoded the future*, and the "reversion toward the
mean" it appears to predict is pure look-ahead (hence the negative IC — the manufactured edge is
spurious mean-reversion toward a peeked-at centre). The expanding mean uses only the past, never
converges to $\bar x_i$ for a non-stationary series, and so leaks nothing.

## The leak scales like a finite-sample artefact — its fingerprint

**It grows with the forward horizon** (a longer forward window overlaps more of the future the
full-sample mean saw), and **it dilutes as the sample lengthens** (each future point is a smaller
share of $\bar x_i$) — both signatures of a look-ahead contamination, not a real effect (10 seeds):

| Forward horizon | full IC | expanding IC | full fake Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | −0.034 | −0.001 | 4.10 |
| 5 days | −0.093 | +0.000 | 11.20 |
| 10 days | −0.138 | −0.001 | 16.05 |
| 20 days | −0.200 | −0.003 | 21.95 |
| 40 days | −0.283 | −0.001 | 28.16 |

| Sample length T | full IC | expanding IC | full fake Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 250 days | −0.275 | −0.004 | 28.63 |
| 500 days | −0.194 | −0.002 | 21.65 |
| 1,000 days | −0.138 | −0.001 | 16.05 |
| 2,000 days | −0.099 | −0.001 | 12.08 |

The expanding-window column stays nailed to zero everywhere — the honest method never sees the
mirage.

## The timer — the fake edge is a Mirage of a different kind

Charging the long-short book to trade (non-stationary null, full-sample signal):

| One-way cost | Gross | Net | Cost/day | Net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 bp | +144.6 bps | +142.5 bps | 2.1 bps | 14.34 |
| 5 bps | +144.6 bps | +134.5 bps | 10.1 bps | 13.53 |

Note the honest caveat: friction does **not** kill this book — a look-ahead Sharpe of ~16 shrugs off
10 bps. That is *why* the Mirage stamp here is about **implementability**, not costs: the signal is
built from the full-sample mean/std, which are only known *after* the last trade in the window. You
cannot run it out-of-sample. Re-standardise point-in-time and the Sharpe collapses from ~16 to ~1
(statistically 0). There was never anything to harvest.

## Why the verdict is what it is

1. **The only "edge" is a look-ahead artefact.** On a random-walk null with provably-unpredictable
   forward returns, full-sample z-scoring manufactures IC −0.138 (*t* −12) and Sharpe ~16 on 20/20
   seeds; the point-in-time method reads exactly 0. There is no real signal. **Signal `NONE`.**
2. **Nothing to trade.** The fake book requires the full-sample mean/std — data from after every
   trade — so it is unimplementable; costs are beside the point. Standardise honestly and it
   vanishes. **Tradability `MIRAGE`.**
3. **The pitfall is confirmed.** Full-sample standardisation genuinely and severely inflates measured
   IC/Sharpe on a non-stationary feature, the leak scales exactly like a finite-sample artefact
   (grows with horizon, dilutes with length), and the honest expanding method both kills it *and*
   still recovers a planted real edge (*t* +22). **`CONFIRMED`.**

## The honest takeaway

Standardisation feels like harmless bookkeeping, so it escapes the look-ahead audit that a
lag-shifted signal would never survive. But z-scoring a **non-stationary** feature with the
**full-sample** mean & std smuggles the future into every historical row, and a backtest will happily
report a Sharpe of 16 for a strategy that is pure noise. The fix is free and non-negotiable: compute
every normalisation statistic on an **expanding / rolling, past-only** window — the same one you could
run live. `NONE` × `MIRAGE`, pitfall `CONFIRMED`. This is a method demo on synthetic worlds by design
— it can never earn `REAL`, which requires a robust *t* ≥ 2 on a real tape.
